purpose: Machine-readable rationale and alternatives for Inttegro demo integration choices.

hosted-web.summary: A trusted merchant server creates and finalizes one order; the payer chooses Inttegro Checkout on its hosted page, embedded in the app, or in an app-owned modal.

native-payment-sheet.summary: A trusted merchant backend creates and finalizes an order; the mobile app receives only the order ID and presents the Inttegro SDK payment sheet.

decisions.selected: Read INTTEGRO_API_KEY only in trusted server code.
decisions.rationale: A distributable browser or mobile bundle cannot keep a merchant credential secret.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production deployments and key rotation.
alternatives.consequences: Inject the key at runtime from a platform secret manager; never expose it through public environment-variable prefixes.

decisions.selected: Use the Inttegro-hosted Checkout experience for payment entry in all three presentations.
decisions.rationale: Inttegro owns payment entry and provider confirmation while the merchant controls whether that experience appears as a page, inline frame, or modal.

alternatives.whenToUse: The product requires a materially custom payment flow and can own every payment state and recovery path.
alternatives.consequences: More UI, state-machine, compliance, payment-method, recovery, and testing responsibility moves to the merchant.

decisions.selected: Let the payer choose embedded, modal, or hosted-page Checkout without changing the server-owned Order operation.
decisions.rationale: The demos compare presentation choices directly while preserving one payment contract, one trust boundary, and a working no-JavaScript path.

alternatives.whenToUse: A production product has already chosen the presentation that best fits its journey.
alternatives.consequences: Render only that option and keep the same server endpoint and progressive fallback where practical.

decisions.selected: Return only the finalized Order ID to clients that mount an Inttegro Checkout surface, with JSON responses marked no-store.
decisions.rationale: The client needs the Order capability to pay, but not the merchant API key, authoritative cart inputs, customer authority, or hosted invoice URL.

alternatives.whenToUse: The browser follows the hosted-page path.
alternatives.consequences: Return an HTTP 303 directly to the URL supplied by Inttegro so no Order reference must be handled by merchant JavaScript.

decisions.selected: Standalone server-framework demos load the fixed, versioned Inttegro runtime URL directly.
decisions.rationale: Rails, Django, Go, Java, and similar examples remain runnable without adding a Node build solely to demonstrate the same browser Checkout contract.

alternatives.whenToUse: After the preview packages are published, a production JavaScript application already has a package build and benefits from typed lifecycle integration.
alternatives.consequences: Install @inttegro/js or the React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular adapter; the package still loads executable code only from Inttegro's fixed origin.

decisions.selected: Derive request_meta.idempotency_key from one logical checkout attempt and reuse it on retry.
decisions.rationale: A retried order-creation request should not create a second successful order.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production carts, invoices, and authenticated checkout attempts.
alternatives.consequences: Persist a key based on a stable merchant identifier and keep the payload unchanged for replays.

alternatives.whenToUse: Only when the operation will never be retried as the same logical intent.
alternatives.consequences: A new request cannot replay the first result, so timeout recovery can create duplicates.

decisions.selected: Send a human-readable merchant order number that is stable for the logical checkout.
decisions.rationale: Without number, Inttegro uses its generated order ID as the order number, which weakens customer-facing labels and merchant reconciliation.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production carts, bookings, invoices, subscriptions, or sales orders.
alternatives.consequences: Use the existing merchant-owned number and persist its mapping to the Inttegro order ID. Keep it unchanged for idempotent retries and exclude customer PII.

alternatives.whenToUse: The merchant has no separate order-numbering system and intentionally wants Inttegro IDs in every customer and operations surface.
alternatives.consequences: Omit number; Inttegro will use the generated order ID as the order number and invoice label fallback.

decisions.selected: Send customer_data for a guest checkout.
decisions.rationale: The demo collects the minimum contact context in the current flow and does not maintain customer accounts.

alternatives.whenToUse: The merchant has repeat customers, saved details, or an account-to-Inttegro customer mapping.
alternatives.consequences: Resolve and authorize the Customer on the server and send customer_id instead; never send both representations.

decisions.selected: Resolve the mobile demo customer ID on the backend.
decisions.rationale: Customer ownership is trusted merchant state and must not be selected by an untrusted app request.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production mobile applications.
alternatives.consequences: Resolve the Inttegro customer from the authenticated merchant principal rather than a global demo environment variable.

decisions.selected: Read Product and Price IDs from trusted deployment configuration and never from the browser or mobile request.
decisions.rationale: Product identity, price identity, currency, and amount are merchant-authoritative commercial data.

alternatives.whenToUse: A production application supports multiple products, variants, or carts.
alternatives.consequences: Accept only a merchant cart or SKU reference, authorize it for the caller, then resolve the Inttegro Product and Price IDs on the server.

decisions.selected: Look up the configured Product during each checkout and verify its configured Price.
decisions.rationale: The demo observes catalog publication and price changes immediately and avoids a second cache state that readers must reason about.

alternatives.whenToUse: Product lookup volume or latency justifies caching.
alternatives.consequences: Use a short TTL and explicit invalidation for publishing, archiving, price activation, currency changes, and catalog rollouts.

decisions.selected: Look up a configured Inttegro Product and Price on the trusted server, validate them, and snapshot their authoritative fields into the Order.
decisions.rationale: The public demo request cannot choose product identity or amount, catalog publication and price changes remain authoritative, and the snapshot works across maintained SDK versions whose typed catalog-reference request shapes are not yet uniform.

alternatives.whenToUse: The Product identity is canonical but the transaction price is calculated by trusted merchant logic.
alternatives.consequences: Send product_id and an explicit price; Inttegro snapshots catalog data into the order.

alternatives.whenToUse: Both Product and Price are maintained in Inttegro and the selected SDK exposes the typed catalog-reference line-item shape.
alternatives.consequences: Send product_id, price_id, and quantity without inline product fields; this is the preferred direct representation once the SDK surface supports it.

alternatives.whenToUse: The merchant owns its catalog outside Inttegro.
alternatives.consequences: Resolve product identity and amount from the merchant database, then send an inline product snapshot; never accept authoritative fields from the browser or mobile client.

decisions.selected: Represent GHS 50.00 as integer value 5000.
decisions.rationale: Inttegro price values use the currency's smallest unit, avoiding ambiguous decimal serialization.

alternatives.whenToUse: A production UI accepts decimal prices or supports currencies with different exponents.
alternatives.consequences: Convert using a decimal or money type and currency metadata; do not use binary floating point.

decisions.selected: Create the complete order with finalize true.
decisions.rationale: The demo total and line items are settled before submission, so one call can freeze the order and generate checkout formats.

alternatives.whenToUse: Shipping, tax, inventory, approval, or line items can change before payment.
alternatives.consequences: Create a draft, update it while mutable, and call the finalize operation only after totals are authoritative.

decisions.selected: Use an HTTP(S) public-origin override, with request origin as a local-development fallback.
decisions.rationale: Inttegro needs externally reachable completion and cancellation URLs, while localhost demos should remain easy to run.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production and any deployment behind a proxy.
alternatives.consequences: Configure a known origin and a precise trusted-proxy chain so untrusted Host headers cannot choose return URLs.

decisions.selected: Read order.invoice.format.web.url from the create-order response.
decisions.rationale: The returned URL is the public contract; constructing a URL couples the merchant to undocumented routing details.

alternatives.whenToUse: An asynchronous invoice flow sends the hosted link through another supported channel.
alternatives.consequences: Persist the order and use the documented invoice operation or returned format instead of inventing a URL.

decisions.selected: Respond to an ordinary or hosted-page form POST with HTTP 303.
decisions.rationale: This preserves a resilient no-JavaScript path: the browser follows the hosted checkout URL with GET and does not replay the merchant form body.

alternatives.whenToUse: A client-rendered flow needs to coordinate UI state before navigation.
alternatives.consequences: Return the URL as data and navigate explicitly, while handling disabled JavaScript and retry behavior.

decisions.selected: Use the returned order ID for correlation; the demo cookie is illustrative only.
decisions.rationale: The merchant needs a stable mapping from its cart, invoice, customer, or tenant to the Inttegro order.

alternatives.whenToUse: Every production integration.
alternatives.consequences: Persist merchant ID, Inttegro order ID, owner, idempotency key, and fulfillment state transactionally.

decisions.selected: Treat redirects and SDK completion callbacks as UX signals, then look up order state on the trusted server before fulfillment.
decisions.rationale: Client returns can be replayed, skipped, delayed, or observed before the authoritative state settles.

alternatives.whenToUse: Current Inttegro integrations because merchant-facing webhooks are not available.
alternatives.consequences: Poll briefly for immediate UX, reconcile non-terminal orders in a background job, and make fulfillment idempotent.

decisions.selected: Map failures to stable, non-sensitive error codes and messages.
decisions.rationale: Raw upstream errors and stack traces can contain internal details and are not a stable public contract.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production support and incident diagnosis.
alternatives.consequences: Return or display a safe correlation ID and keep detailed diagnostics in access-controlled server telemetry.

decisions.selected: Use AsyncInttegroClient whenever the framework executes checkout work on an event loop.
decisions.rationale: Awaitable SDK I/O preserves framework concurrency and is compatible with runtimes such as Cloudflare Python Workers that do not provide blocking outbound sockets.

alternatives.whenToUse: A synchronous framework, script, management command, or worker owns the call stack.
alternatives.consequences: Use InttegroClient directly; do not call the synchronous client from an async handler unless the runtime provides and permits a bounded thread offload.

decisions.selected: Reuse one async client for the lifetime of the server process or isolate, then close it during framework shutdown.
decisions.rationale: A long-lived transport can reuse connections and keeps lifecycle ownership visible at the application boundary.

alternatives.whenToUse: Strict tenant isolation or request-specific transport configuration outweighs connection reuse.
alternatives.consequences: Construct and close the client inside the request lifetime so sockets are released deterministically.

decisions.selected: Keep framework routes and integration services unchanged while a narrow runtime adapter translates the deployment platform's request boundary.
decisions.rationale: One checkout implementation is easier to audit and test than a second provider-specific handler with independent payment behavior.

alternatives.whenToUse: The target runtime cannot execute the framework contract or the provider version intentionally offers different product behavior.
alternatives.consequences: Treat it as a separate application, duplicate the security and contract tests, and document the behavioral differences explicitly.

decisions.selected: Read Cloudflare bindings at the Worker boundary and apply framework security settings before application initialization.
decisions.rationale: Python Worker bindings are not ordinary process environment variables, while frameworks such as Django freeze important settings during import.

alternatives.whenToUse: A container or process platform injects secrets into the environment before starting the application.
alternatives.consequences: Read the values through the framework's normal configuration path and validate them before accepting traffic.

decisions.selected: Consume bounded SDK telemetry without customer data, secrets, or raw payloads.
decisions.rationale: Operational correlation is useful while payment and customer data require strict minimization.

alternatives.whenToUse: A server application has an existing tracing pipeline.
alternatives.consequences: Configure the application provider at startup; the SDK does not choose an exporter or observability vendor.

decisions.selected: The app sends only an attempt ID to the merchant backend and receives only an order ID.
decisions.rationale: Products, prices, customer ownership, allowed payment methods, and credentials remain server-owned.

alternatives.whenToUse: Production mobile applications or an existing merchant API gateway.
alternatives.consequences: Authenticate the principal, authorize the cart, add rate limiting and abuse controls, and return a minimal checkout projection.

decisions.selected: Initialize the Inttegro SDK with a finalized order ID and registered return URL, then present its payment sheet.
decisions.rationale: The SDK owns native payment-method presentation while the app retains its product experience.

alternatives.whenToUse: The application intentionally prefers a browser-based checkout or cannot include a native SDK.
alternatives.consequences: Use the hosted URL and a secure browser surface, then preserve the same server-side verification boundary.
